mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 3% signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 3%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressure and input costs, reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE < 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 2% signals stronger manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where INDPRO 3-month growth > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below -2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where GDPC1 3-month growth < -2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% signals a loosening labor market, which reduces wage pressure and input costs, boosting profit margins and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where UNRATE 3-month growth > 0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% and a monthly increase in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals a tight labor market with rising wage costs, reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% AND PAYEMS 1-month growth > 0.5%
regime_hint: tight labor market with rising wage costs
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS 1-month growth > 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
